## Scope

CHORALE compares latent factors estimated in modalities measured on different individuals. It does
not claim to recover a unique biological state or the unobserved joint distribution of modalities.
Its cross-modal result is a phenotype-led factor correspondence with empirical error control.

## Factor extraction

For modality (m), the standardised sample-by-feature matrix is approximated as

\[
X_m = S_m A_m^T + E_m .
\]

FastICA estimates scores (S_m) and loadings (A_m) separately in each modality. Phenotype and
covariates are not used here. Starts are aligned by maximum absolute score correlation; the medoid
start, which has the greatest mean agreement with the other aligned starts, is retained.

## Adjusted design effects

Let (y_{mk}) be the score of factor (k) in modality (m). CHORALE fits

\[
y_{mk}=D_m\beta_{mk}+\varepsilon_{mk},
\]

where (D_m) contains an intercept, phenotype contrasts, and all eligible shared secondary
covariates. The reported phenotype coefficient is therefore adjusted for those covariates.

Continuous variables enter as standardised slopes. A categorical variable enters as a treatment-
contrast block using common levels. For secondary covariate (c), its (q_c)-coefficient block is
scaled by (1/\sqrt{q_c}). Thus every secondary covariate has equal total block weight. Coefficient
covariance matrices come from the fitted multivariable model.

## Phenotype affinity and orientation

For factors (k) and (l), phenotype coefficient vectors (b_{mk}) and (b_{nl}), and their
estimated variances (v_{mk}) and (v_{nl}), CHORALE compares the two possible ICA orientations:

\[
L^+_{kl}=\operatorname{mean}\frac{(b_{mk}-b_{nl})^2}{v_{mk}+v_{nl}},\qquad
L^-_{kl}=\operatorname{mean}\frac{(b_{mk}+b_{nl})^2}{v_{mk}+v_{nl}}.
\]

The smaller loss selects orientation. Affinity combines this compatibility loss with the phenotype
signal-to-noise present in both factors. A simultaneous spectral synchronisation uses every pairwise
affinity block to produce one cycle-consistent assignment.

## Candidate sets and hierarchical refinement

Rows are bootstrap-resampled within declared exchangeability blocks. In each replicate, adjusted
effects and phenotype losses are recomputed while ICA remains fixed. For each alternative,
CHORALE records its excess loss over the best candidate. An alternative is removed only when the
lower endpoint of its bootstrap excess-loss interval is above zero.

Secondary affinity compares adjusted effects using their pooled uncertainty, separately for each
covariate block, and averages the block scores. It is evaluated only among retained phenotype
candidates. A high secondary affinity outside the candidate set has no route into the final
assignment.

The resulting state is resolved, ambiguous, phenotype unsupported, or incompatible, as defined in
the outputs vignette.

## Phenotype support and family-wise control

Phenotype support uses a Freedman--Lane null. A reduced model keeps secondary covariates, phenotype
residuals are permuted within exchangeability blocks, and the full phenotype-led assignment and
modality-subset search are repeated with fixed ICA factors. Each replicate contributes the maximum
statistic reached across the search. Therefore

\[
p = \frac{1 + \#\{T_b^{\max}\ge T_{obs}\}}{B+1}
\]

controls the family-wise error rate for that search. No subsequent BH correction is applied to the
same p-values.

## Pathway channel

Pathway evidence is analysed separately. Scores are residualised on the shared design, residual rows
are permuted, and loadings are recalculated against the unchanged assay matrix. This preserves
feature correlation and annotation structure. The maximum pathway statistic calibrates the pathway
search. Because both channels use the fitted factors, pathway and design evidence are not assumed
independent.

## Coupling bounds

Without paired individuals, marginal score distributions do not select one correlation. CHORALE
optimises correlation over couplings compatible with those marginals, optionally within shared
design strata. The output is an identified range ([L,U]), not a point estimate.

Bootstrap resampling rebuilds containers, refits ICA, aligns re-estimated factors to the original
factors, and recomputes endpoints. The resulting endpoint range is called a sensitivity envelope
until simulation establishes confidence coverage.

## Gates and diagnostics

Production gates concern phenotype estimability, common design support and rank, factor stability,
factor detectability, permutation support, and assignment ambiguity. Distributional shape checks
and pure-feature statistics are diagnostics. No theoretical recovery claim or discovery threshold
is inferred from those diagnostics.

## Main limitations

- A correspondence is about factors, not unobserved measurements in the same individual.
- Strong secondary agreement cannot compensate for absent phenotype evidence.
- Bounds can remain wide even when a factor correspondence is well supported.
- Pathway interpretation depends on annotation coverage.
- Sensitivity envelopes do not yet have claimed confidence coverage.
